images.title: Pancreatic lobules and ducts, phase-contrast view
images.description: Cross section of human pancreas at 100x magnification by phase contrast, with a haematoxylin and eosin stain listed in the source. Dark granular acinar lobules are divided by pale connective tissue septa, and a large round duct or vessel with grey contents lies near the centre-right. Students should find the lobules, the septa and the larger round profiles that are ducts or vessels.
images.author: Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library

images.title: Islet of Langerhans among exocrine acini
images.description: Cross section of human pancreas at 200x magnification, with the haematoxylin and eosin stain listed in the source. A pale islet of Langerhans fills the centre of the field, with lightly stained cells and round nuclei, while the surrounding acini are darker purple and more granular. Students should compare the paler endocrine cells of the islet with the acinar cells around it, and note the thin septa between lobules.
images.author: Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library

images.title: Large islet of Langerhans among acini (phase contrast)
images.description: Cross section of human pancreas at 100x magnification by phase contrast, with a haematoxylin and eosin stain listed in the source. A large, pale islet of Langerhans lies in the centre, surrounded by dark granular acini, and smooth pale round and elongated profiles, probably ducts or vessels, lie at the right and lower edge. Students should find the islet and the acini around it, and tell the islet apart from these larger ducts or vessels.
images.author: Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library

images.title: Two islets of Langerhans among acini (phase contrast)
images.description: Cross section of human pancreas at 200x magnification by phase contrast, with a haematoxylin and eosin stain listed in the source. Two pale islets of Langerhans sit among the darker acini, one at the upper left and one at the lower centre, and a pale connective tissue septum runs diagonally across the field. Students should compare the loosely packed, pale islet cells with the granular acinar cells around them.
images.author: Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library

images.title: Pancreatic lobules with septa and a small islet
images.description: Cross section of human pancreas at 100x magnification, with a haematoxylin and eosin stain listed in the source. Dark blue-purple acinar lobules are separated by thin pale septa, and a paler, slightly granular islet of Langerhans lies within one lobule near the centre-left. Larger smooth pale profiles, probably ducts or blood vessels, sit at the lower left; students should find the islet and these larger profiles among the lobules.
images.author: Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library

images.title: Islet of Langerhans among acini at low power
images.description: Cross section of human pancreas at 40x magnification, with a haematoxylin and eosin stain listed in the source. A pale islet of Langerhans lies in the upper centre of the field among purple acinar lobules, and pale round profiles, probably ducts or vessels, sit near the lower centre. Students should find the islet against the surrounding acini, and the thin pale septa dividing the lobules.
images.author: Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library

images.title: Islets of Langerhans beside large pale ducts or vessels
images.description: Cross section of human pancreas at 100x magnification, with a haematoxylin and eosin stain listed in the source. A large, pale islet of Langerhans sits at the top centre, with a second islet lower down in the centre, and both are paler than the darker purple acini around them. Elongated pale profiles, probably ducts or blood vessels, run across the centre and lower right; students should compare the islets with these and with the acinar lobules.
images.author: Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library

tissues.name: Nasal & olfactory mucosa
tissues.summary: The nasal mucosa lines the nasal cavity, where respiratory epithelium warms, humidifies and filters inhaled air. A patch of olfactory epithelium in the roof of the cavity detects odours.
features: Respiratory region: pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells
Large venous plexuses (swell bodies) in the lamina propria
Olfactory epithelium in the roof: bipolar olfactory neurones, sustentacular and basal cells
Bowman glands beneath the olfactory epithelium, which wash odorants from the surface

images.title: Sagittal diagram of the nasal cavity showing the regions of each mucosa type
images.description: A labelled sagittal diagram of the nasal cavity, not a microscope image, colour-coding its mucosa: squamous at the nostrils (green), respiratory over the turbinates (blue), olfactory in the roof next to the cribriform plate (yellow), and NALT near the tonsils and nasopharynx (red). It shows where each mucosa type lies, which the stained slides cannot show.
images.author: Stella Gänger and Katharina Schindowski

images.title: Human olfactory epithelium with axon bundles and Bowman glands (H&E)
images.description: A haematoxylin and eosin section of human olfactory epithelium with a 100 micrometre scale bar. The thick, densely nucleated epithelium lies above a dashed line marking the basement membrane, and the lamina propria below holds axon bundles and Bowman gland acini. Find the basement membrane, the axon bundles and the glands.
images.author: Tanos T, Saibene AM, Pipolo C, Battaglia P, Felisati G, Rubio A

images.title: Engraved section of olfactory mucous membrane with Bowman glands
images.description: A black and white line engraving of a section through the olfactory mucous membrane, credited to Cadiat in the source, with no stain or magnification given. The epithelium lies along the top, with nerve bundles at the left and right and clusters of Bowman glands in the lamina propria below. It is a useful layout diagram for finding the glands and nerve bundles under the epithelium.
images.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

tissues.name: Larynx & vocal folds
tissues.summary: The larynx is a cartilage-supported airway between the pharynx and trachea that protects the lower airway during swallowing and houses the vocal folds that produce voice. Its lining changes from respiratory epithelium in the vestibular folds to non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium over the true vocal folds, which withstands the mechanical stress of vocal fold vibration.
features: True vocal fold: non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium over a dense vocal ligament and the vocalis muscle
Reinke space: loose superficial lamina propria under the vocal fold epithelium, which swells in Reinke oedema
Vestibular (false) folds: respiratory epithelium with seromucous glands
Hyaline cartilage of the thyroid, cricoid and arytenoid cartilages
Epiglottis: elastic cartilage core with chondrocytes in lacunae within branching elastic fibres

images.title: Small artery and vein in the epiglottic mucosa, with wall layers labelled
images.description: Transverse section through a small artery and vein in the mucous membrane of a child's epiglottis, shown as a black-and-white line engraving at the magnification given in the source (X 350). The stain is not stated and cannot be judged from the drawing. In the artery (lower), a student should find the lining endothelium (e), the thick circular smooth-muscle media (m) and the outer adventitia (a); the thin-walled vein (upper, V) has a much thinner media.
images.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

tissues.name: Trachea
tissues.summary: The trachea is the cartilage-supported airway that carries air between the larynx and the bronchi, with C-shaped hyaline cartilage rings keeping its lumen open. Its lining is pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells, whose cilia move mucus upwards.
features: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells on the luminal surface
Thick basement membrane beneath the epithelium (thickened in asthma)
Seromucous glands in the submucosa
C-shaped hyaline cartilage rings, with perichondrium and chondrocytes in lacunae
Trachealis smooth muscle bridging the open back of each C-ring

images.title: Trachea wall: labelled section of lining, glands and cartilage
images.description: Labelled OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology figure of a section through the trachea wall, with no magnification given; the pink and purple colours suggest H&E. Students should find the pseudostratified columnar epithelium with cilia facing the lumen, the submucosal seromucous glands, and the hyaline cartilage at the lower left.
images.author: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology

images.title: Trachea lining and glands in a digital photo through a microscope
images.description: Author's own digital camera photograph through a microscope of human trachea, as the source states, with no stain or magnification given. A folded lining of respiratory epithelium runs across the top, dark submucosal glands sit at the right edge, and fibrous tissue lies beneath, with a dark probe across part of the field.
images.author: Jpogi at Wikipedia

images.title: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with labelled cell types
images.description: Light micrograph of a transverse section of trachea at 50x, as the source states, with no stain given; the teal collagen in the lamina propria suggests a trichrome-type stain. Labels mark ciliated cells (C), goblet cells (G), basal cells (B) and the basement membrane (BM), which show the layers of the pseudostratified epithelium.
images.author: Eugeenia Wen

images.title: Whole trachea ring in low-power H&E section
images.description: Low-power H&E-stained cross-section of the whole trachea, as the source states, with no magnification given. The thick purple wall is mainly hyaline cartilage around a central lumen, with the thinner mucosa and submucosa along the inner edge.
images.author: Alexander Klepnev

images.title: Hyaline cartilage with perichondrium and epithelial lining, H&E
images.description: Low-power H&E section, which the source describes as an elastic artery seen in light microscopy; the stain matches but the content does not. It shows a large lilac plate of hyaline cartilage with scattered chondrocytes, wrapped in a pink perichondrium, with a purple epithelial lining at the right edge. This pattern is more typical of the trachea wall, so the image is misfiled under elastic artery.
images.author: Otávio Astor Vaz Costa

tissues.name: Bronchi
tissues.summary: The bronchus is an intrapulmonary airway that carries air between the trachea and the bronchioles. Its wall has a pseudostratified ciliated columnar lining, irregular cartilage plates, spirally arranged smooth muscle and submucosal glands.
features: Irregular plates of hyaline cartilage in the wall, instead of C-shaped rings
Spiral bands of smooth muscle between the mucosa and the cartilage
Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells
Submucosal mucous and serous glands with their ducts
Bronchus-associated lymphoid tissue in the mucosa and submucosa
Chronic bronchitis: enlarged submucosal glands (raised Reid index)

images.title: Cross-section of a secondary bronchus through a microscope eyepiece
images.description: Phone photo taken through a microscope eyepiece of a cross-section of a secondary bronchus, stained pink and purple (probably H&E); no magnification is given in the source. The lumen is largely empty, a black rod crosses the right-hand wall and the image is soft, so the wall layers are hard to tell apart.
images.author: Jpogi at English Wikipedia

tissues.name: Bronchioles
tissues.summary: Bronchioles are the small airways, usually under 1 mm across, that carry air deep into the lung without cartilage or glands. Their wall contains a relatively thick layer of smooth muscle that controls airway calibre, and terminal bronchioles lead on into respiratory bronchioles, where alveoli open and gas exchange begins.
features: No cartilage in the wall, unlike bronchi
No submucosal glands
Relatively thick ring of smooth muscle around the lumen
Ciliated simple columnar epithelium with club (Clara) cells, flattening to cuboidal in terminal bronchioles
Respiratory bronchioles with alveoli opening from their walls

images.title: Respiratory zone diagram: terminal bronchiole, alveolar ducts and sacs
images.description: Labelled English-language illustration of the respiratory zone from the Anatomy and Physiology material on the Connexions website. It shows a terminal bronchiole with smooth muscle in its wall, the respiratory bronchiole, the alveolar duct, the alveolar sac with alveolar pores, and the capillaries around the alveoli, with deoxygenated blood from the pulmonary artery and oxygenated blood to the pulmonary vein. It is a diagram rather than a microscope image, so no stain or magnification applies.
images.author: OpenStax College

tissues.name: Lung alveoli
tissues.summary: The lung alveoli are the millions of thin-walled air sacs where oxygen and carbon dioxide pass across the air-blood barrier, giving the lungs a gas-exchange surface of roughly 70 m². Their walls are lined mainly by flat type I pneumocytes, while type II cells secrete surfactant.
features: Thin alveolar septa around open air spaces, lined by flat type I pneumocytes (about 95% of the surface)
Cuboidal type II pneumocytes at the corners of alveoli, which secrete surfactant
Capillaries packed with red blood cells within the septa
Alveolar macrophages ('dust cells') in the air spaces, which may be full of haemosiderin in heart failure
Bronchioles with alveoli opening off them, and pores of Kohn joining neighbouring alveoli

images.title: Bronchiole and alveolar ducts, annotated with letter labels
images.description: Annotated section of normal lung tissue from patients with hamartochondroma, with an H&E-type stain; no magnification is given. It shows a bronchiole with its lumen, and the alveoli and alveolar ducts around it, and the figure carries arrows and letters (P, M, BT, PB, DA, A, AS) with no key. Students should find the folded bronchiolar lumen, the wall around it and the alveoli beyond.
images.author: Anhenn O et al. (published in BMC Infect Dis, v.4; 2004), modified by Christian2003

images.title: Airway wall diagram: trachea or bronchus, without and with inflammatory cells
images.description: Two-panel diagram of the wall of a trachea or bronchus, labelled for mucus, goblet cells, epithelium, basement membrane, lamina propria, smooth muscle, glands and cartilage. Panel (b) adds mast cells, macrophages, eosinophils and neutrophils to the lamina propria. It is an unstained diagram of the conducting airway, not of the alveoli, so students should not confuse it with alveolar tissue.
images.author: OpenStax College

images.title: Respiratory zone: labelled alveoli, alveolar duct and sac
images.description: Labelled section of the respiratory zone of lung, with an H&E-type stain (pink and purple); the source gives no magnification. Text labels mark alveoli, an alveolar duct, an alveolar sac, blood vessels and the lumen of a bronchiole. Students should use them to tell the thin alveolar walls from the airway lumen and the vessels.
images.author: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology

tissues.name: Kidney cortex & glomerulus
tissues.summary: The renal cortex is the outer zone of the kidney, made up mainly of renal corpuscles and the convoluted parts of the nephron tubules. Here blood is filtered at the glomeruli, and the tubules then reabsorb and secrete substances to form urine.
features: Renal corpuscle: round glomerular capillary tuft inside a pale Bowman's space
Proximal convoluted tubule: eosinophilic cells with a brush border and a fuzzy lumen
Distal convoluted tubule: smaller, paler cells with a clear, open lumen
Macula densa: tall, crowded distal tubule cells at the vascular pole of the glomerulus
Basement membranes: PAS stain outlines the capillary loops and capsule in magenta

images.title: Kidney section in a light micrograph with a strong orange tint
images.description: Light micrograph of kidney tissue with a strong orange tint and dark vignetting around the edge of the field. Round profiles that may be tubule cross-sections or glomeruli are faintly visible, but the detail is too soft to identify structures reliably, and the stain and magnification are not stated.
images.author: Borislav Yanev

images.title: High-power kidney section labelled as juxtaglomerular cells
images.description: Digital camera photo through a microscope at high magnification, with pink cytoplasm and purple nuclei that suggest H&E (the source does not name the stain). Cells with round nuclei line a large clear lumen, and a dark needle-like object crosses the lower centre, but the granular JG cells in an arteriole wall are not clearly identifiable at this resolution.
images.author: Jpogi

images.title: Kidney cortex at low power with several glomeruli among tubules
images.description: Author's own digital camera photo of kidney cortex through a microscope, in a pink and purple stain that looks like H&E (the source does not name it). Several renal corpuscles are scattered among the tubules, each a round tuft with a pale Bowman's space. A dark needle-like artefact crosses the centre of the field, and no magnification is given.
images.author: Jpogi at English Wikipedia

images.title: Diagram of glomerular cell types: mesangial cell, capillaries and podocytes
images.description: Coloured schematic, not microscopy, of the cells in a glomerulus: a central mesangial cell, capillary loops with red blood cells and an endothelial lining, and podocytes with their foot processes around the outside. The source describes it as showing podocytes, endothelial cells and mesangial cells. Students should use it to match each cell type to its position relative to the capillary loops.
images.author: Artwork by Holly Fischer

images.title: Diagram of kidney blood supply through glomeruli, arteries and veins
images.description: Coloured schematic, not microscopy, of kidney blood flow with arteries in red and veins in blue. It shows glomerular capillary tufts fed from a vertical artery and drained to a vertical vein, plus a U-shaped loop of vessels at the bottom that resembles the vasa recta of the medulla. It gives the vascular context for the cortex but does not show cell detail.
images.author: Artwork by Holly Fischer

images.title: Kidney cortex at low power: glomeruli and renal tubules
images.description: Pink-stained section seen through a microscope eyepiece, appearing to show renal cortex at low power. The source gives no stain or magnification, but the pink colour suggests an eosin-based stain. Several round glomeruli sit among many cut tubule profiles, and the thin parietal layer of Bowman's capsule cannot be resolved at this power, so the image belongs with the kidney cortex tissue.
images.author: Naz Amann

tissues.name: Kidney medulla & collecting system
tissues.summary: The kidney medulla is the inner zone of the kidney, made of renal pyramids that contain the loops of Henle, collecting ducts and vasa recta. It concentrates urine by building a salt gradient through the interstitium, which draws water out of the collecting ducts.
features: Collecting ducts: cuboidal to columnar cells with distinct borders, around wide lumens (principal and intercalated cells)
Thin limbs of Henle: very thin walls that look like capillaries but contain no red blood cells
Vasa recta: thin-walled capillaries running parallel to the tubules, often with red blood cells in the lumen
Papillary ducts: large, tall columnar ducts that open onto the renal papilla into a minor calyx

images.title: Renal medulla: tubules cut in cross-section
images.description: Renal medulla in a stained microscope section, with many tubules cut in cross-section and separated by a thin interstitium. The section appears to be H&E stained, with purple nuclei and pink cytoplasm. Students should look for the open lumens ringed by cuboidal to low columnar epithelial cells with round central nuclei, and the thin pink interstitium between the tubules.
images.author: Pathologist without beard

tissues.name: Ureter
tissues.summary: The ureter is a muscular tube that carries urine from the renal pelvis to the bladder. Its lumen is lined by urothelium (transitional epithelium), and peristaltic smooth muscle in the wall propels the urine onward.
features: Star-shaped lumen: the mucosa is thrown into folds, so the lumen looks stellate in cross-section
Transitional epithelium (urothelium) lining the lumen as a multilayered purple band that follows every fold
Lamina propria: loose connective tissue filling the core of each fold, beneath the epithelium
Thick smooth muscle wall: inner longitudinal and outer circular layers, with an extra outer longitudinal layer lower down
Outer adventitia of loose connective tissue, with fat and small blood vessels around the wall

images.title: Ureter in transverse section: low-power view with labelled wall layers
images.description: Labelled low-power micrograph of a transverse section of the ureter, H&E-stained in pink and purple. The folded mucosa forms a star-shaped lumen surrounded by a thick smooth muscle wall, with loose connective tissue and some fat outside. Students should find the lumen, the mucosal folds, the smooth muscle layer and the adventitia at the edge.
images.author: OpenStax College

images.title: Ureter lumen: urothelial lining and underlying connective tissue, close view
images.description: Close-up photograph taken through a microscope with a digital camera, showing the lumen of the ureter. The lumen is star-shaped and bordered by a thin, dark purple urothelial lining, with pink connective tissue beneath it. The stain appears to be H&E, and students should see the thin lining following each fold.
images.author: Jpogi at English Wikipedia

images.title: Ureter wall layers in transverse section: labelled line drawing
images.description: Labelled line drawing of a transverse section of the ureter, with the lumen and folded epithelium at the centre and the wall layers around it. The labels mark the epithelium, the connective tissue beneath it, the mucosa as a whole, the muscular layer and the adventitia. The labels are in Portuguese, but the structures match the English drawings.
images.author:
Gray's Anatomy

derivative work: User:Faduart

images.title: Ureter wall in transverse section: engraved drawing of the tissue layers
images.description: Line drawing of a transverse section of the ureter, with the lumen lined by transitional epithelium. The labels mark the subepithelial connective tissue, the longitudinal and circular muscle fibres and the fibrous tissue at the outside. Students should find the epithelium, the two muscle layers and the outer fibrous tissue.
images.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

images.title: Ureter wall layers in transverse section: labelled drawing with urothelium
images.description: Line drawing of a transverse section of the ureter that appears to be the same drawing as the English-labelled version, with the labels in Serbian. The labels mark the outer connective tissue layer, the longitudinal and circular muscle layers, the lamina propria and the urothelium. Students should use it to see how the wall layers stack around the lumen.
images.author: Author not recorded on Wikimedia Commons (see source page)

images.title: Ureter wall: schematic of fibrous coat, muscular coat and mucosa
images.description: Simplified coloured schematic of a block of ureter wall, with the fibrous coat at the top, the muscular coat below it and the mucosa drawn as folded tissue at the base. It is a diagram rather than a microscope image, but the layers are in the correct order from outside to inside. Students should use it to learn how the wall layers stack.
images.author: Author not recorded on Wikimedia Commons (see source page)

tissues.name: Urinary bladder
tissues.summary: The urinary bladder is a hollow, distensible reservoir that stores urine until it is voided. Its wall is lined by transitional epithelium (urothelium) over a lamina propria and a thick detrusor of interlacing smooth muscle, and the lining flattens as the bladder fills.
features: Transitional epithelium (urothelium): stratified lining several cells deep
Umbrella cells: large, often binucleate surface cells that cover the lumen
Lining thins and flattens when distended, and is thick and folded when collapsed
Lamina propria: loose connective tissue with spindle-shaped nuclei beneath the urothelium
Detrusor: thick smooth muscle layer of interlacing bundles cut in several planes

images.title: Normal urothelial intermediate cells in Pap-stained cytology
images.description: Normal intermediate urothelial cells in cytology, stained with Pap stain, which gives cyan cytoplasm and dark blue nuclei; the source gives no magnification. Students should look for flat, polygonal cells with sharp borders and round nuclei of fairly even size, which form the normal reference for judging abnormal urothelial cells.

images.title: Bladder diagram with transitional epithelium histology inset, Spanish labels
images.description: The same bladder diagram as the English version, with Spanish labels, showing the ureters, peritoneum, detrusor muscle, ureteral openings and the internal and external urethral sphincters. images.title: Bladder diagram with transitional epithelium histology inset, English labels
images.description: A labelled diagram of the bladder showing the ureters, peritoneum, detrusor muscle, ureteral openings and the internal and external urethral sphincters, with an H&E-stained section of the wall as an inset. The inset shows transitional epithelium over lamina propria and submucosa. Students should find these three layers in the inset and relate them to the thick detrusor in the diagram.

images.title: Bladder wall layers: line drawing of urothelium, submucosa and three muscle layers
images.description: A line drawing of a cross-section of the bladder wall, with Serbian labels for the urothelium, submucosal layer and the inner, middle and outer muscular layers. As a drawing it has no stain or magnification. Students should match each drawn layer to its name and note that the detrusor is organised into three muscle layers here.
images.author: Author not recorded on Wikimedia Commons (see source page)

tissues.name: Urethra
tissues.summary: The urethra is the tube that carries urine from the bladder to the outside of the body, and in males it also carries semen. Its lining changes along its length, from urothelium (transitional epithelium) near the bladder to stratified squamous epithelium at the external opening.
features: Prostatic urethra: urothelium (transitional epithelium) with rounded surface cells
Membranous and spongy urethra: pseudostratified or stratified columnar epithelium
Navicular fossa and external opening: stratified squamous epithelium
Mucous glands of Littré opening into the lumen of the spongy urethra
Smooth muscle coat outside the lamina propria; in males the spongy urethra sits in erectile tissue with venous sinusoids

tissues.name: Pancreatic islets of Langerhans
tissues.summary: Islets of Langerhans are small clusters of hormone-secreting endocrine cells scattered through the exocrine pancreas. They release insulin, glucagon, somatostatin and pancreatic polypeptide directly into the blood to regulate blood glucose.
features: Pale, rounded clusters of endocrine cells scattered among darker exocrine acini
Islet cells with round nuclei and pale cytoplasm, unlike the granular acinar cells around them
Dense capillary network running between the islet cells
Beta cells (insulin) form most of the islet and lie centrally; alpha cells (glucagon) lie at the periphery, best shown by immunostaining
Type 1 diabetes: lymphocytes infiltrate the islets (insulitis); type 2: amyloid deposits (amylin) form within islets

images.title: Pancreatic islets among blood vessels packed with round cells
images.description: Cross section of human pancreas, H&E stain, 200x magnification by phase contrast, as given in the source. Pale islets are scattered among the darker, granular exocrine acini, and two vessels are packed with round cells, most likely red blood cells. Students should find the pale islet cells with round nuclei and compare them with the surrounding acini.
images.author: Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library

images.title: Islet of Langerhans in the human pancreas, phase contrast
images.description: Cross section of human pancreas, H&E stain, 200x magnification by phase contrast, as given in the source. A central islet of pale cells with round nuclei sits among the darker exocrine acini that surround it. Students should trace the edge of the islet and compare its loosely arranged, paler cells with the compact acini.
images.author: Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library

images.title: Larger islets of Langerhans near interlobular ducts in the human pancreas
images.description: Cross section of human pancreas, H&E stain, 40x magnification, as given in the source. Lobules are separated by pale connective tissue septa, and several larger islets show as paler clusters within the purple acini. Students should scan this low-power view to find the paler islets among the acini and the septa that divide the lobules.
images.author: Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library

images.title: Small peripheral islets of Langerhans in the human pancreas
images.description: Cross section of human pancreas, H&E stain, 100x magnification by phase contrast, as given in the source. Small islets appear as pale clusters among the darker exocrine acini. Students should compare the pale islet cells with the surrounding acinar tissue at this higher magnification and find their round nuclei.

tissues.name: Pituitary gland
tissues.summary: The pituitary gland is a small endocrine gland at the base of the brain with two main lobes. The glandular anterior lobe (pars distalis) makes GH, prolactin, ACTH, TSH, FSH and LH, while the neural posterior lobe (pars nervosa) stores and releases ADH and oxytocin made in the hypothalamus.
features: Anterior lobe (pars distalis): cell clusters of acidophils (pink cytoplasm), basophils (purple cytoplasm) and pale chromophobes
Capillaries packed with red blood cells running between the anterior lobe cell clusters
Posterior lobe (pars nervosa): pale, sparsely cellular neural tissue of unmyelinated axons and pituicytes
Herring bodies: swollen axon endings in the posterior lobe that store ADH and oxytocin
Pars intermedia: a thin band of cells between the lobes, sometimes with colloid-filled Rathke cysts

tissues.name: Thyroid gland
tissues.summary: The thyroid gland is an endocrine organ made of closed follicles, each lined by cuboidal cells that make thyroglobulin and store it as colloid, from which the hormones T3 and T4 are released. Parafollicular C cells between the follicles secrete calcitonin.
features: Follicles lined by simple cuboidal epithelium, taller when active and flatter when resting
Pale colloid in the follicle lumen, with scalloped margins and resorption vacuoles at the edge when active
Parafollicular C cells (calcitonin) between follicles, often paler than the follicular cells
Graves disease: tall, hyperplastic follicular cells with scalloped colloid
Hashimoto thyroiditis: dense lymphocytic infiltrate, lymphoid follicles and Hürthle cells

tissues.name: Parathyroid gland
tissues.summary: Parathyroid glands are usually four small endocrine glands on the back of the thyroid. Their chief cells secrete parathyroid hormone, which raises blood calcium levels.
features: Chief cells in cords, nests and sheets, with round nuclei and pale cytoplasm
Rich capillary network between the cell cords, often with red blood cells in the lumen
Oxyphil cells: larger, with pink (eosinophilic) cytoplasm and many mitochondria; increase with age
Clear adipocytes between the cell nests, increasing with age
Fibrous capsule and septa, with larger vessels running through the fibrous tissue

tissues.name: Adrenal (suprarenal) gland
tissues.summary: The adrenal (suprarenal) gland sits on the upper pole of each kidney. Its outer cortex makes steroid hormones in three zones (glomerulosa, fasciculata and reticularis), and its inner medulla, a modified sympathetic ganglion, makes adrenaline and noradrenaline.
features: Zona glomerulosa: thin outer band of small cell clusters under the capsule (aldosterone)
Zona fasciculata: widest zone, cords of pale, lipid-rich cells (cortisol)
Zona reticularis: branching cords of cells with lipofuscin pigment (androgens)
Medulla: clusters of chromaffin cells around thin-walled sinusoids (adrenaline, noradrenaline)
Central adrenomedullary vein running through the medulla

images.title: Adrenal gland: whole section with the zones and central vein labelled (Arabic labels)
images.description: A whole-section micrograph of the adrenal gland, with Arabic labels that (translated) mark the fibrous capsule, the zona glomerulosa, zona fasciculata, zona reticularis, the medulla and the large central adrenomedullary vein. The source describes it as showing the cortex and medulla, the three cortical zones and the central vein. The stain is not given, but the blue-green capsule suggests a trichrome-type stain.

images.title: Adrenal gland: whole section labelled with the zones, medulla and central vein
images.description: A whole-section photograph of a human adrenal gland taken through a microscope, labelled in English for the fibrous capsule, the three cortical zones, the medulla and the central adrenomedullary vein. The stain is not stated, but the blue-green capsule suggests a trichrome-type stain. The labels make it a good check on the zones against the outline of the whole gland.
images.author: Jpogi

images.title: Adrenal gland: unlabelled whole section from capsule to central vein
images.description: A whole-section view that appears to be the same as the English-labelled image, with no labels added and a dark rod-shaped object across the top edge. images.title: Adrenal gland: outer cortex close to the capsule, with fat beyond the edge

images.title: Adrenal gland: capsule, cortex and medulla in one purple-stained field
images.description: A purple-stained view, probably trichrome, with a dark rod-shaped object at the top, showing the blue-green capsule along the top edge, the cortical cells beneath it and the medulla lower down. images.title: Adrenal gland: outer cortex under the capsule, with medulla and vessels below

tissues.name: Pineal gland
tissues.summary: The pineal gland is a small endocrine organ in the roof of the diencephalon that secretes melatonin from pinealocytes arranged in lobules. Calcified brain sand (corpora arenacea) accumulates with age and serves as a useful radiological landmark.
features: Pinealocytes in lobules, with round nuclei and pale cytoplasm
Interstitial astrocytes with elongated nuclei in the septa between lobules
Corpora arenacea (brain sand): dark calcified concretions that increase with age
Fibrous septa and a rich capillary bed dividing the lobules
Calcified pineal is a radiological midline landmark on skull X-ray and CT

images.title: Rat pineal gland at embryonic day 21: Pax6 and vimentin immunofluorescence
images.description: Confocal immunofluorescence of a sagittal section through the rat pineal gland at embryonic day 21, with Pax6 nuclei in green and vimentin in red. Panel G1 (20x, 75 µm scale bar) shows the gland as a compact, rounded mass of Pax6-positive cells surrounded by vimentin-rich tissue, while G2 to G4 (60x, 25 µm scale bar) show individual nuclei and vimentin fibres. A student should see that by this stage the gland is a recognisable globular structure.
images.author: María P. Ibañez Rodriguez, Stephen C. Noctor, Estela M. Muñoz

images.title: Vole brain near the pineal gland: interlaced blood vessels, modified azan stain
images.description: Light micrograph of a longitudinal section through the brain of the northern red-backed vole (Clethrionomys (Myodes) rutilus) in the area of the pineal gland, stained with modified azan. Blood vessels show as orange-yellow bands that interlace through the blue-stained brain tissue, so this is a vascular view of the region rather than typical pinealocyte lobules. Students should note the vessel network and treat it as context around the gland.
images.author: Stranger

images.title: Rat pineal gland, embryonic day 15 to 21: Pax6 and vimentin series
images.description: Confocal immunofluorescence series of sagittal sections through the developing rat pineal gland from embryonic day 15 to day 21, with Pax6 in green and vimentin in red, at 20x with a 75 µm scale bar. The gland is a thin, curved band at E15 and E16 that thickens into a rounded mass by E21. Labels mark the third ventricle (3v), posterior commissure (PC) and subcommissural organ (SCO) near the gland, and the series shows how it develops from neuroepithelium.
images.author: María P. Ibañez Rodriguez, Stephen C. Noctor, Estela M. Muñoz

images.title: Human pineal gland at 40x: pinealocyte lobules with brain sand
images.description: Cross section of human pineal gland stained with haematoxylin and eosin at 40x magnification. Several dark, calcified concretions of brain sand (corpora arenacea) lie among purple-stained pinealocyte clusters, separated by pale stroma. images.title: Human pineal gland at 100x: brain sand in pinealocyte clusters

images.title: Human pineal gland at 100x: two large concretions of brain sand
images.description: Cross section of human pineal gland stained with haematoxylin and eosin at 100x magnification. images.title: Human pineal gland at 200x: brain sand concretion among pinealocytes
images.description: Cross section of human pineal gland stained with haematoxylin and eosin at 200x magnification. images.title: Human pineal gland by phase contrast at 100x: brain sand fragments

A cluster of dark, calcified brain sand fragments (corpora arenacea) sits among pinealocytes, outlined by a pale halo typical of phase optics. The phase contrast makes the fragments and cell outlines stand out, so students can compare it with the bright-field images.

images.title: Human pineal gland by phase contrast at 200x: single brain sand concretion
images.description: Cross section of human pineal gland imaged by phase contrast at 200x magnification, with a haematoxylin and eosin stain. images.title: Human pineal gland at 100x: pinealocyte lobules wrapped in connective tissue
images.description: Cross section of human pineal gland stained with haematoxylin and eosin at 100x magnification. images.title: Young human pineal gland at 100x: densely packed pinealocytes
images.description: Cross section of young human pineal gland stained with haematoxylin and eosin at 100x magnification. images.title: Young human pineal gland at 40x: dense cellular parenchyma
images.description: Cross section of young human pineal gland stained with haematoxylin and eosin at 40x magnification. images.title: Young human pineal gland at 100x: pinealocytes with pale stroma

images.title: Young human pineal gland by phase contrast at 100x: dense cell population
images.description: Cross section of young human pineal gland imaged by phase contrast at 100x magnification, with a haematoxylin and eosin stain. The field is densely packed with small, darkly stained nuclei, with paler spaces between them, and the strong contrast makes the cell outlines easy to see. Students can use it to judge the cellular density of the young gland against the older glands with brain sand.

tissues.name: Testis
tissues.summary: The testis is the male gonad, where seminiferous tubules produce sperm through spermatogenesis, supported by Sertoli cells. Leydig cells in the interstitial tissue between the tubules secrete testosterone.
features: Seminiferous tubules: round cross-sections with a central lumen, packed closely together
Germ cells in layers: spermatogonia at the base, spermatocytes above, spermatids near the lumen
Sertoli cells: tall supporting cells with large nuclei and a prominent nucleolus, joined by tight junctions (blood-testis barrier)
Leydig cells: clusters in the interstitial tissue between tubules, making testosterone (Reinke crystals on electron microscopy)
Peritubular myoid cells: flattened cells outside the basal lamina of each tubule
Tunica albuginea: thick fibrous capsule around the whole organ

images.title: Human testis: cross-section schematic and labelled seminiferous tubule
images.description: Two-part figure: panel A is a labelled diagram of the whole testis, showing lobules, seminiferous tubules, rete testis, efferent ducts, tunica albuginea and epididymis. Panel B is a micrograph of one seminiferous tubule that looks H&E stained, with no magnification given, and the figure labels its spermatogonia, primary and secondary spermatocytes, spermatids and Sertoli cells.

images.title: Mink seminiferous tubule with labelled Sertoli, Leydig and germ cells
images.description: Light micrograph of a seminiferous tubule from a mink testis, stained with H&E and fixed in modified Davidson's fluid as the source states, with a 20 µm scale bar. Letters mark a Sertoli cell (S), a round spermatid (R), a Leydig cell (L) in the interstitium and a pachytene primary spermatocyte (PP), and students should also find the dark, elongating spermatid heads near the lumen.
images.author: Ellinor Spörndly-Nees, Elisabeth Ekstedt, Ulf Magnusson, Azadeh Fakhrzadeh, Cris L. Luengo Hendriks, Lena Holm

images.title: Naked mole-rat testis: Sertoli and early germ cells in electron microscopy
images.description: Six electron micrographs (panels A to F) from Heterocephalus glaber, the naked mole-rat, showing a Sertoli cell crowded with fluid-filled vesicles and its nucleolus (A), dividing Sertoli cells (B), A and B spermatogonia (C), and leptotene, early pachytene and mid-pachytene primary spermatocytes (D to F). As electron micrographs they have no light stain and the scale bars run from 2 to 10 µm, and students should note the Sertoli nucleolus and the paired chromosomes in mid-pachytene nuclei.
images.author: van der Horst G, Kotzé SH, O’Riain MJ and Maree L

images.title: Human seminiferous tubules in cross-section at low power
images.description: Camera photograph taken through a microscope eyepiece, showing many cross-sections of human seminiferous tubules packed together, with pale lumens and thin interstitial tissue between them. The source gives no stain or magnification, and the pink colour is consistent with H&E but this is not confirmed. Students can use it to recognise tubule profiles and lumens, although the cell layers are too blurred to identify cell types.

images.title: Sertoli cell tight junctions blocking lanthanum tracer in electron microscopy
images.description: Three electron micrographs (panels A to C) of control and SCARKO testes at 35 days old, showing that lanthanum tracer is stopped by the tight junctions between Sertoli cells, which form the blood-testis barrier. Panel A has a boxed area with an arrow to the junction, panel B enlarges it, and panel C shows tight junction 'kissing points' (white arrowheads) inside an ectoplasmic specialisation. Black arrowheads mark lanthanum beneath the junction, and the scale bars are 2 µm, 500 nm and 100 nm.

images.title: Stage XI seminiferous tubule: Sertoli cells and basal lamina in electron microscopy
images.description: Two electron micrographs labelled Stage XI (panels H and I) from hamster testis, stained with anti-GDNF antibody using DAB and osmium black, as the source describes. images.title: Sertoli cell nuclei with nucleoli, bat testis, electron microscopy
images.description: Electron micrograph from panel b of a figure on germ cells at stage 1 of the seminiferous epithelial cycle in Sturnira lilium, a bat, in the dry season. It shows two Sertoli cell nuclei (SC) with dense nucleoli (asterisks), with interstitial tissue (I) at lower left and the basal lamina marked by an arrow. The source gives a 2 µm scale bar.

images.title: Sertoli cell surface beside spermatogonia, GDNF labelled, electron microscopy
images.description: Electron micrograph from Figure 6 of the source, from hamster testis with anti-GDNF staining (DAB and osmium). images.title: Stage XI tubule: Sertoli cells and spermatogenic cells in electron microscopy
images.description: Panel H of the Stage XI electron micrograph from hamster testis, the same picture as panel H in the other Stage XI image in this set, shown here at a larger size. It shows Sertoli cells (S), spermatogenic cells (G) and a peritubular myoid cell at the basal lamina (asterisk), with a 1 µm scale bar in the source.

images.title: Sertoli cell nuclei (red) and Leydig cells (green) by immunofluorescence
images.description: Immunofluorescence micrograph from Figure 3 of the source, from adult Cyp26b1 SC-/SC- animals, with GATA-1 antibody in red marking Sertoli cell nuclei and 3β-HSD antibody in green marking Leydig cells. The source reports germ cell loss in this model, but this panel shows only the two marker stains. The scale bar is 20 µm.

tissues.name: Epididymis
tissues.summary: The epididymis is a highly coiled duct along the back of each testis where sperm mature, gain the ability to swim and fertilise, and are stored until ejaculation. Its lining is pseudostratified epithelium, surrounded by a thin smooth-muscle coat that thickens towards the tail.
features: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium with long stereocilia projecting into the lumen
Principal cells, the main cell type, forming most of the tall epithelial lining
Basal cells: small cells resting on the basement membrane, beneath the principal cells
Lumen filled with sperm, seen as dark heads and tails
Thin smooth-muscle layer around each duct, thickening towards the tail

images.title: Epididymis tubules at low power, photographed through a microscope
images.description: A photograph of a circular microscope field showing epididymal tubules at low power, with a hair lying across the field and no magnification given. Many tubules are cut in cross-section or coiled, with pale lumens and a darker purple lining, set in connective tissue. The image is small and soft, so students should use it only to see the overall tubule pattern rather than fine cell detail.
images.author: Abdulrazakca

images.title: Mouse efferent ducts and initial segment of the epididymis, H&E
images.description: H&E-stained section of the proximal epididymis from control mice aged two months, shown at low power with a scale bar of 1.5 mm as given in the source. The efferent ducts (ED) are the smaller profiles along the upper edge, and the initial segment (IS) is the larger central region of coiled tubules. Students should compare the small efferent duct profiles with the wider tubules of the initial segment.
images.author: Björkgren I., Saastamoinen L., Krutskikh A., Huhtaniemi I., Poutanen M., Sipilä P.

images.title: Schematic of epididymal cell types and epididymosome release
images.description: A schematic diagram rather than a micrograph, showing the epididymal epithelium with principal cells that release apical blebs, along with basal, clear, narrow and halo cells and spermatozoa in the lumen. An inset shows an epididymosome, a small membrane vesicle carrying membrane fusion proteins, nucleic acids and other proteins. Students should use it to match each cell type to its appearance in stained sections, not as a picture of a real section.
images.author: Emma R. James , Douglas T. Carell , Kenneth I. Aston , Timothy G. Jenkins , Marc Yeste , Albert Salas-Huetos

images.title: E-cadherin staining of a developing mouse epididymal duct
images.description: Fluorescence image of whole tissue from a mouse epididymis at embryonic day 16.5, stained for E-cadherin, a cell adhesion protein. The bright outlines are the borders between epithelial cells lining a curving duct, and the dark openings are the lumen, with the head and tail ends of the duct marked. The source gives a scale bar of 50 µm and notes that the image is a single-section view, so students should focus on the cell borders.
images.author: Hirashima T., Adachi T.

images.title: Initial segment and caput of the mouse epididymis, H&E
images.description: H&E-stained section of the adult control mouse epididymis (two months old), with a dashed line dividing the initial segment (IS) on the left from the caput (CAP) on the right. The source states the IS has tall columnar epithelial cells, averaging about 45 µm high, while the caput epithelium is low; the scale bar is 100 µm. Students should compare the tall epithelium of the initial segment with the low epithelium of the caput.
images.author: Björkgren I., Saastamoinen L., Krutskikh A., Huhtaniemi I., Poutanen M., Sipilä P.

images.title: Caput epididymis at electron microscopy with sperm in the lumen
images.description: Electron micrograph of the caput epididymis from a wild-type mouse, with a scale bar of 2 µm, and the source gives no stain. Spermatozoa are evident in the lumen (Lu) at the top, and below them lie principal cells (P), a non-ciliated cell (NC) and a basal cell (BC), with a myoid layer (My) beneath the epithelium and intertubular space (IT) outside. Students should find the sperm in the lumen and the thin myoid layer under the epithelium.
images.author: Oliveira R., Hermo L., Pshezhetsky AV., Morales CR.

images.title: Halo cell and basement membrane in the efferent duct, electron micrograph
images.description: Electron micrograph of the efferent duct from a wild-type mouse, with a scale bar of 500 nm. A halo cell (HC) with two dense lysosomes (L) sits above the basement membrane (BM), and a myoid cell (My) lies below it. Students should find the halo cell and its dense lysosomes, and see how the basement membrane separates the epithelium from the myoid layer.
images.author: Oliveira R., Hermo L., Pshezhetsky AV., Morales CR.

images.title: Efferent duct epithelium with ciliated and non-ciliated cells, electron micrograph
images.description: Electron micrograph of the efferent duct from a wild-type mouse, with a scale bar of 2 µm. The lumen (Lu) lies at the top, with a ciliated cell (C) beside non-ciliated cells (NC) packed with small to medium dense lysosomes (L). Students should compare the ciliated and non-ciliated cells, and find the myoid cell (My) layer below the epithelium.
images.author: Oliveira R., Hermo L., Pshezhetsky AV., Morales CR.

images.title: Schematic of epididymal epithelial cell types with sperm in the lumen
images.description: A schematic diagram, not a micrograph, of the epididymal epithelium with principal cells, basal, narrow, clear and dendritic cells, and apical blebs releasing epididymosomes into the lumen where spermatozoa lie. Microvilli line the luminal surface. Students should use it to match each cell type to its appearance in stained sections, and note that the apical blebs on principal cells release epididymosomes.
images.author: Zhou W., De Iuliis GN., Dun MD., Nixon B.

images.title: Four segments of the mouse epididymis with H&E sections of each
images.description: Panel A is a schematic of the mouse epididymis showing the initial segment, caput, corpus and cauda, and panel B shows a section from each segment that looks H&E-stained, with no magnification given. The source notes that the initial segment is a slightly coiled, wide tubule with tall stereocilia and few sperm, the caput has a narrow lumen, and lumen diameter and sperm number increase towards the corpus and cauda. Students should compare the four sections to see the lumen widen and fill with sperm along the duct.
images.author: Zhou W.; De Iuliis GN.; Dun MD.; Nixon B.

tissues.name: Ductus deferens
tissues.summary: The ductus (vas) deferens is a muscular duct that carries sperm from the epididymis to the ejaculatory duct, moving them along by peristaltic contraction of its thick smooth muscle wall. Its narrow lumen is lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium with stereocilia, and the wall is much thicker than the lumen.
features: Narrow, irregular lumen with folded mucosa, small compared with the wall
Very thick smooth muscle wall in three layers: inner longitudinal, middle circular, outer longitudinal
Pseudostratified columnar epithelium with stereocilia lining the lumen
Loose adventitia outside the muscle wall, with small vessels and nerves

images.title: Vas deferens in cross-section at low power: thick muscle wall, small lumen
images.description: Low-power H&E cross-section of an unremarkable vas deferens; the source gives no magnification. tissues.name: Seminal vesicle
tissues.summary: The seminal vesicles are a pair of highly coiled glands lying behind the bladder. Their folded, secretory lining produces a fructose-rich, alkaline fluid that makes up most of the ejaculate volume.
features: Highly coiled, branching mucosal folds giving a honeycomb or labyrinthine pattern
Pseudostratified or cuboidal lining epithelium, often with yellow-brown lipofuscin pigment
Lumen filled with pale or eosinophilic secretion between the folds
Thick smooth-muscle wall around the folded mucosa
Loose connective tissue between lobules, with small blood vessels

images.title: Seminal vesicle at low power, several lobules with branching folds
images.description: Microscope field at 4x, as given in the source, showing several seminal vesicle lobules cut in section, each made of a labyrinth of branching mucosal folds around pale lumens. The stain appears to be H&E, with purple epithelium and a thick pink muscular wall around each lobule. Students should find the branching folds, the lumen between them, and the blood vessels in the connective tissue between lobules.

images.title: Seminal vesicle mucosal folds in close-up
images.description: Photograph taken through a microscope by the author, as stated in the source, of a cross-section through a human seminal vesicle, shown as a close-up of pink-stained folds with pale lumens between them. tissues.name: Prostate
tissues.summary: The prostate is a male accessory sex gland made of branching tubuloalveolar glands set in a fibromuscular stroma that surrounds the urethra just below the bladder. Its glandular epithelium secretes a fluid that forms part of semen.
features: Papillary infoldings of the gland lining, giving folded lumens
Two cell layers: tall luminal cells over flattened basal cells
Corpora amylaceum: layered concretions in gland lumens
Fibromuscular stroma: smooth muscle and collagen between glands
Missing basal cell layer (p63-negative glands) is a key sign of carcinoma

tissues.name: Penis & erectile tissue
tissues.summary: The penis consists of three erectile bodies: the paired corpora cavernosa and the single corpus spongiosum that surrounds the urethra. Each is a mass of endothelium-lined vascular spaces enclosed by a tunica albuginea, and these spaces fill with blood to produce an erection.
features: Corpora cavernosa: endothelium-lined blood spaces (sinusoids) separated by smooth-muscle trabeculae
Corpus spongiosum: similar blood spaces packed around the urethra, which runs through its centre
Trabeculae: connective tissue with elastic fibres and bundles of smooth muscle, forming the stroma between the spaces
Tunica albuginea: a thick, dense capsule enclosing each erectile body
Helicine arteries: tightly coiled small arteries within the trabeculae that dilate during erection

images.title: Corpus cavernosum, non-distended: trabeculae and blood sinuses (engraving)

tissues.name: Mammary gland
tissues.summary: The mammary gland is a branched tubuloalveolar gland that secretes milk during lactation, organised into terminal duct lobular units within fibrous and fatty stroma. Its acini and ducts have an inner luminal epithelium and an outer myoepithelial layer, which contracts to push milk out.
features: TDLU: a terminal duct with its acini, the site of most breast cancers
Two-cell lining: luminal epithelial cells inside, myoepithelial cells outside
Loose intralobular stroma within lobules vs dense interlobular stroma between them
Pink eosinophilic secretion in the acinar lumen
Lactation: distended alveoli filled with lipid-rich secretion and hobnail epithelium

tissues.name: Ovary
tissues.summary: The ovary is the female gonad, producing oocytes and the hormones oestrogen and progesterone. Its cortex holds follicles at every stage of development around a vascular medulla, and each ovulation leaves a corpus luteum that later regresses to a corpus albicans scar.

Follicles at every stage: primordial, primary, secondary and Graafian (antral)
Theca interna makes androgens; granulosa cells convert them to oestrogen
Corpus luteum after ovulation, later replaced by a pale corpus albicans scar
Vascular medulla: loose stroma packed with blood vessels at the centre

images.title: Mammalian ovary at low power with vessels and stroma
images.description: Low-power light micrograph of mammalian ovary at x50 magnification, as the source states. Dense pink stroma fills most of the field, with a blood vessel containing red blood cells in the lower centre. The source does not name the stain, and the pink and blue colouring is what is seen.
images.author: Eugeenia Wen

images.title: Corpus albicans: pale scar tissue in ovarian stroma
images.description: Digital camera photo through a microscope of a human corpus albicans, the scar left when a corpus luteum regresses. Pale, hyaline, sparsely cellular areas stand out against the denser pink stroma, and small blood vessels are scattered throughout. The source gives no stain or magnification; the pink and purple colouring suggests H&E.
images.author: Jpogi

images.title: Primary follicle with oocyte and granulosa cells
images.description: Digital camera photo through a microscope of a human primary follicle, with pink and purple staining, probably H&E; the source gives no magnification. A central oocyte with a faint nucleus is ringed by a thick pink zona pellucida, with two or more layers of granulosa cells around it. Spindle-shaped stroma surrounds the follicle.
images.author: Jpogi at English Wikipedia

images.title: FOXL2 staining of granulosa cells in primary and antral follicles
images.description: Figure from a research paper showing FOXL2 immunohistochemistry as brown nuclear staining, with a schematic of follicle growth at left. Panel A shows a primary follicle and panel D an antral follicle, where granulosa cell nuclei are strongly stained; the source gives a 100 µm scale bar. The caption also covers GATA4 and SMAD3 and panels B, C, E and F, which are not in this image.
images.author: Mikko Anttonen, Marjut Pihlajoki, Noora Andersson, Adrien Georges, David L'Hôte, Sanna Vattulainen, Anniina Färkkilä, Leila Unkila-Kallio, Reiner A. Veitia, Markku Heikinheimo

images.title: Developing genital ridge with primitive ova and Müllerian ducts
images.description: A line drawing, not a stained slide, after Waldeyer, labelled as a section through the urogenital fold of a chick embryo on the fourth day. It shows the genital ridge with primitive ova and ovarian stroma, the Wolffian duct and tubules, and the Müllerian duct. It belongs with ovary development rather than tonsil.
images.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

images.title: Newborn ovary cortex: primordial follicles beneath germinal epithelium
images.description: A line drawing, labelled in Arabic, of a section through the ovary of a newly born child, after Waldeyer. It shows the surface germinal epithelium, primordial follicles with oocytes surrounded by follicle cells, cellular stroma, a blood vessel and a developing follicle. It belongs with the ovary, not the tonsil.
images.author: Henry Vandyke Carter

tissues.name: Uterine tube
tissues.summary: The uterine tube (fallopian tube) is a paired muscular tube that carries the oocyte from the ovary to the uterus, and the ampulla is the usual site of fertilisation. Its mucosa forms highly branched folds lined by ciliated and secretory peg cells, surrounded by inner circular and outer longitudinal smooth muscle.
features: Highly branched mucosal folds that project into the lumen, most elaborate in the ampulla
Tall columnar epithelium with apical cilia, which beat to move the oocyte
Non-ciliated secretory peg cells between the ciliated cells, which nourish the oocyte
Thick muscular wall of inner circular and outer longitudinal smooth muscle

images.title: Uterine tube: ciliated columnar epithelium at high magnification
images.description: High-power view of the tubal lining: tall columnar epithelial cells with nuclei at different levels and a fringe of cilia on the free surface, sitting on loose lamina propria with elongated stromal nuclei. The source gives no magnification; the pink and purple colours suggest H&E. Students should find the cilia, the columnar nuclei and the underlying stroma.

images.title: Uterine tube wall: mucosal folds above the muscular wall
images.description: Author's own photograph, taken with a digital camera through a microscope, of a human uterine tube wall. Folded mucosa with its lumen occupies the upper right, while the fibrous muscular wall runs diagonally across the lower left. The source gives no stain or magnification; students should find the mucosal folds, the lumen between them and the wall beneath.
images.author: Jpogi at English Wikipedia

images.title: Fimbria of the uterine tube: schematic and micrograph
images.description: Two-panel teaching figure: a schematic of the fimbria cut by horizontal lines marking the planes of section, and an arrow leading to a micrograph of the fimbriated mucosa in section. The source describes the micrograph as the uterine tube pavilion (fimbria) and gives no stain or magnification; the micrograph appears to be H&E stained. The micrograph is small, so students should look for the branching folds and their lumens.
images.author: Sanador2.0

images.title: Uterine tube cross-section with folded lumens and surrounding fat
images.description: Cross-section of the uterine tube with folded mucosa around two lumen profiles, set in a thick, dense muscular wall. Fat cells and small vessels lie outside the tube at the upper left. The source gives no description, stain or magnification; the colours suggest H&E, and students should find the folded lumens, the muscular wall and the fat outside the tube.
images.author: Ciência e Saúde XXI

tissues.name: Uterus (endometrium & myometrium)
tissues.summary: The endometrium is the mucosal lining of the uterus, made of simple columnar epithelium, tubular glands and a cellular stroma that sits on a thick smooth-muscle myometrium. Its functional layer is shed at menstruation and regenerated each cycle, and in the secretory phase it is prepared for embryo implantation.
features: Simple columnar surface epithelium lining the uterine cavity
Tubular glands in a cellular stroma; narrow and straight in the proliferative phase
Secretory phase: dilated, coiled glands with secretion in their lumens
Decidualised fibroblasts with abundant pale cytoplasm near spiral arterioles
Immune cells, likely macrophages and uterine NK cells, in the functional layer
Thick myometrium of interlacing smooth muscle beneath the endometrium

images.title: Simple columnar surface epithelium of the endometrium
images.description: Section through the luminal surface of the endometrium, showing a single layer of tall columnar cells across the top of the field. A tubular gland dips down into the loose stroma beneath, and stromal cells lie between the glands. H&E stain; no magnification is given.

images.title: Secretory endometrium with dilated glands and decidualised stroma
images.description: H&E micrograph of secretory endometrium with a 500 micrometre scale bar and in-figure labels. Prominent glands (G) have dilated lumens and an irregular outer border stretching down into the basal compartment, and the luminal surface runs across the top. Decidualised fibroblasts (DEC) lie close to arterioles, and immune cells, most likely macrophages and uterine natural killer cells, are seen in the functional layer.
images.author: Douglas A. Gibson, Ioannis Simitsidellis, Frances Collins and Philippa T.K. Saunders

tissues.name: Cervix
tissues.summary: The cervix is the narrow, lower part of the uterus that forms a canal between the uterine cavity and the vagina. Its endocervix is lined by mucus-secreting columnar epithelium, while the ectocervix facing the vagina is covered by non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium, and the two meet at the transformation zone.
features: Endocervix: simple columnar mucus-secreting epithelium lining branching glands and clefts
Ectocervix: non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium, with nuclei still present in the superficial cells
Transformation zone: the junction where squamous and columnar epithelium meet, the site where HPV-related dysplasia arises
Nabothian cysts: mucus-filled spaces where an obstructed endocervical gland has dilated

images.title: Transformation zone: mucus-filled gland within squamous epithelium
images.description: Transformation zone of the cervix, where stratified squamous epithelium meets mucus-secreting glands; the section shows a mucus-filled gland sunk within squamous mucosa. H&E stain. Students should find the layered squamous epithelium around the gland, the pale, vacuolated mucin in its lumen and the lining cells of the gland wall.

images.title: Ectocervix: non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium
images.description: Ectocervix, the outer part of the cervix, showing full-thickness stratified squamous epithelium in section, from the superficial flattened cells down to the basal layer on the stroma. H&E stain. Students should note that the superficial cells still contain nuclei (non-keratinised), the paler intermediate cells with clear cytoplasm and the dark basal layer.
images.author: Manuel Medina from Osuna, España

images.title: Ectocervix: squamous epithelium with a ridge dipping into stroma
images.description: Ectocervical squamous epithelium in section, with the basal layer forming a downward ridge at one side over a broad, pink fibrous stroma. H&E stain. Students should look for the dark basal cell line, the downward ridge of epithelium on the right and the many small blood vessels with red blood cells in the stroma beneath.
images.author: Manuel Medina from Osuna, España

images.title: Ectocervix: squamous epithelium with rounded cell nests in its base
images.description: Ectocervical stratified squamous epithelium in section, with flattened superficial cells and small rounded nests of cells with central lumens in the lower epithelium. H&E stain. Students should find the thin superficial layer with nuclei still present, and the deeper, darker-staining layers of basal and parabasal cells.
images.author: Manuel Medina from Osuna, España

labels.text: Rounded cell nest with central lumen

images.title: Ectocervix: squamous epithelium with cell clusters around lumens
images.description: Ectocervical squamous epithelium in section, with nucleated superficial cells above rounded clusters of cells around lumens in the lower epithelium. H&E stain. Students should look for the flattened, nucleated surface cells, the dark basal cell layer at the base and the stroma below it.
images.author: Manuel Medina from Osuna, España

images.title: Ectocervix: squamous epithelium with dark cell clusters at the base
images.description: Ectocervical stratified squamous epithelium in section, showing the flattened superficial layer above paler intermediate cells and darker clusters of cells at the base. H&E stain. Students should identify the nucleated superficial cells, the paler intermediate layer and the small blood vessels in the stroma below.
images.author: Manuel Medina from Osuna, España

images.title: Epithelium types along the female reproductive tract (schematic)
images.description: Schematic diagram, not a micrograph, of the epithelium along the female reproductive tract from oviduct to vagina, with the cervix shown between the uterus and vagina. It marks the columnar endocervix, the transition zone and the stratified squamous ectocervix, alongside stroma, smooth muscle and mesothelium. Students should trace where columnar endocervical epithelium changes to squamous epithelium at the transition zone.
images.author: Jia Shuai and Fei Zhago

tissues.name: Vagina
tissues.summary: The vagina is a muscular, glandless canal lined by thick, non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium that is rich in glycogen. It receives the penis during intercourse and forms the lower part of the birth canal, and its moisture comes from cervical mucus and fluid that seeps through the wall rather than from glands.
features: Thick non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium whose surface cells keep their nuclei
Pale, glycogen-filled cytoplasm in the intermediate cells (glycogen shows with PAS stain)
Epithelium folded into ridges (rugae), with lamina propria filling each fold
Lamina propria rich in elastic fibres and thin-walled veins
No glands in the wall; a thick smooth muscle layer lies beneath the lamina propria

images.title: Vaginal wall: folded stratified squamous epithelium over lamina propria
images.description: Photograph taken through a microscope of a human vaginal wall in H&E stain (appears so; no magnification given). The thick squamous epithelium is thrown into ridges, with pale lamina propria filling the folds and wavy bundles of smooth muscle forming the lower part of the wall. A dark instrument enters from the left, but the layered epithelium and the thin-walled vessels in the lamina propria are still clear.
images.author: Jpogi at English Wikipedia

tissues.name: Placenta
tissues.summary: The placenta is the fetomaternal organ in which fetal chorionic villi project into maternal blood in the intervillous space, allowing exchange of gases, nutrients and wastes. The villi are covered by syncytiotrophoblast, which secretes hCG and separates fetal capillaries from maternal blood.
features: Villi covered by syncytiotrophoblast (secretes hCG) over a layer of cytotrophoblast
Cytotrophoblast layer becomes discontinuous in later pregnancy
Fetal capillaries packed with red cells in the villous stroma
Hofbauer cells (fetal macrophages) in the villous core
Decidual cells on the maternal side, in the basal plate

images.title: Decidual cells with scattered maternal white cells
images.description: Decidua from a miscarriage specimen, H&E stain, 400X as stated in the source. Large polygonal decidual cells with abundant pale cytoplasm and round nuclei fill the field, and small dark leukocytes lie between them. Students should look for the big pale decidual cells and the dark, lobed maternal white cells among them.

images.title: Schematic of a term placenta with floating villi and insets
images.description: Labelled teaching diagram of a term placenta (37 to 40 weeks gestation), showing the chorionic plate, amniotic membrane, floating villi, umbilical cord and extravillous trophoblast in the decidua, with insets A to E. The insets show the amniotic membrane, chorionic plate, placental villi, an anchoring villus and a vessel in the basal plate. Students should find the syncytiotrophoblast covering the floating villi and the sinusoids inside the terminal villi.
